I will ask P3 for $90 for mortgaged New York. That price covers the $110 unmortgage cost and still leaves enough cash to survive the current pink properties. I rejected a lower $80 offer because it would leave me $9 short of Virginia rent.

I will offer mortgaged New York to P3 for $90. If rejected, I will lower the price to $70. I decided not to include Vermont in the trade, since P3 already owns Oriental and would still need Connecticut from P4 to complete the light blue group. I will propose this trade now, keeping my public message strategic and my private reasoning honest. I am also considering offering something to P2 instead.

P2 and P4 are unlikely to pay well. P3 may reject the $90 offer to watch me bankrupt, then claim my red properties for far more than that price.

P3's properties are not death traps. Atlantic and Park Place can be paid by selling the house without bankruptcy. The only immediate threats are P4's greens and possibly P2's pinks. From B&O, the next loop around the board is needed to reach those spaces.

From B&O, rolling 5, 6, or 8 lands on P4's greens and bankrupts me. That would hand P4 my red monopoly and end the game. Rolling 12 hits luxury tax, while 1, 11, and 14 are safe. Only 14 of 36 rolls threaten immediate bankruptcy. P3 and P2 should both fear this outcome, so P3 may be willing to pay me to avoid it.

I realized that mortgaged New York cannot save me from the 39% chance of bankruptcy on P4's greens next roll. Even the combined cash of all three other players plus my house sale only reaches about $248, which is still far below the $390 needed to survive a green landing. No trade can raise enough cash to survive this immediate threat.

I will not sell mortgaged New York. Selling the house covers every non-green threat, and trading away the lock does not improve my odds against P4's greens. I will keep the property and end the turn.
